metadata.title: Translation and adaptation processes in TALIS 2018

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD working paper is not an empirical student-level analysis of TALIS 2018 achievement outcomes; it assesses translation/adaptation and verification procedures using documentation and country survey responses. As such, there is no analytic micro-dataset for which TALIS sampling weights (e.g., student/school weights) or replicate weights would be applied to estimate population-representative statistics. The paper describes TALIS 2018 instrument preparation workflows for the field trial and main survey (eAssessment vs Microsoft Word), including roles of national centres, national project managers, verifiers, and international quality observers. For any future empirical analyses using TALIS micro-data, analysts should apply the official TALIS complex survey weights provided in the international database and follow the TALIS technical documentation for scaling and variance estimation; however, this paper itself does not conduct such weighted estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because the paper does not model TALIS cognitive achievement outcomes using PV-based scales; instead, it evaluates translation/adaptation and verification processes and reports qualitative/administrative outcomes (e.g., reported difficulties, documentation practices, and procedural recommendations). Missing-data handling for PVs or item nonresponse is therefore not part of the study’s analytic design. The paper relies on documentation review and country survey responses about procedures, rather than on a PV-based measurement model requiring explicit PV and missing-data procedures.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The paper does not define an analytic student sample from TALIS 2018 micro-data. Instead, it (i) analyzes available documentation on TALIS 2018 implementation (e.g., SOP3-related procedures, technical report materials, verification documentation) and (ii) administers a separate survey to a purposively selected set of countries that faced translation problems or had good translation practices. It reports that 14 countries were identified and asked to respond, plus a 15th country for French linguistic adaptations; five countries could not answer or answered partially, and additional countries were added, resulting in responses from 15 countries covering 16 language versions with 3 incomplete surveys.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education Working Paper evaluates the translation, adaptation, and verification processes used for TALIS 2018 instruments, drawing on documentation analysis and country-reported experiences. It contrasts the field trial (FT) workflow—using the eAssessment system—with the main survey (MS) workflow—using Microsoft Word and national adaptation forms (NAFs), and it summarizes how verifiers applied sentence-by-sentence checks with severity codes and how post-verification decisions were documented. The paper reports that most countries found verifier checks useful, but that adaptation/translation work was time-consuming and sometimes difficult due to software constraints, tight timelines, and challenges in identifying/recording adaptations. It also highlights recurring issues around trend items, the need for clearer guidelines (including item-by-item guidance), and the value of a translatability assessment introduced for TALIS 2024. Overall, the study’s contribution is procedural: improving comparability depends on earlier detection of translation problems, better documentation tools, and more structured guidance for translators, reviewers, and trend handling.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a procedural/documentation assessment rather than an empirical predictive ML study on TALIS micro-data. Consequently, there is no student-level outcome variable, no PV-based achievement modeling, no ML algorithm evaluation, and no country-by-country student sample size table to extract. The paper’s evidence base is qualitative/administrative (documentation review and country survey responses about translation/adaptation workflows), so fields like total_students, countries with n_students, and main_findings structured as predictive effects are not applicable.
